relatedSnapshot.title: Stop a retried email send from reaching the customer twice
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When background work sends an email and something goes wrong after the mail provider has already accepted it, that work can run again. This gives CRM a durable record of an attempted send, so a second attempt can never put a second copy in the customer's inbox.

## Problem

Texts already have this protection: a record claimed before the phone provider is contacted, so a repeat attempt finds the earlier one instead of sending again. Email has nothing equivalent. CRM writes an email down after the provider confirms it, which recovers a lost record but does nothing to stop a repeat send. That is tolerable while a person is clicking Send, because a person does not silently run twice. It is not tolerable for a scheduled send, where the work can be retried, a hold can expire, and another job can pick the same message up.

## Proposed fix

Give email the same durable record texts already have. Claim the send before the provider is contacted. A later attempt that finds the send already claimed, or already finished, reads what happened the first time instead of sending. An unclear answer from the provider is recorded as unclear and is never resolved by sending again.

## What's included

* A durable record of an email send attempt, marked so that the same logical send always produces the same marker.
* Claiming before the provider is contacted, and recording the result once an answer is known.
* Reading back an earlier result: finished, still in progress, or unclear.
* Keeping a clear failure and an unclear answer separate.

Not included: any user of this. Nothing routes through it yet; the scheduled email sender is its first caller. Changing how Send now behaves is out of scope, and so is the cold email and AI SDR sending path, which has its own duplicate-send work in Send-step idempotency.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately.

## How it should work

* Nothing reaches Gmail or Microsoft until the send has been claimed.
* A second attempt carrying the same marker never contacts the provider. It reads what happened the first time.
* A claim whose owner died partway can be taken again safely, because the provider is contacted at most once per marker regardless.
* An unclear answer stays unclear. Nothing turns it into a send.
* Every read and write belongs to one workspace.

## Who can do what

Not applicable: this slice adds nothing a person can trigger. Every record belongs to one workspace and cannot be read or written from another.

## What the user sees

Not applicable: this slice adds no screen and changes nothing a person can see.

## Done when

- [ ] Contacting the mail provider requires a send claimed first.
- [ ] Two attempts carrying the same marker contact the provider at most once.
- [ ] A claim whose owner died can be taken again without a second send.
- [ ] A finished send returns its recorded result instead of sending.
- [ ] A clear failure and an unclear answer end in visibly different states.
- [ ] A record belonging to another workspace can never be read or written.
- [ ] Tests cover each of the above.

## Open questions

* Whether the existing immediate Send now and Reply should also route through this. Recommended default: not in this release. It changes live behaviour for every rep, gains little while a person is the trigger, and belongs with Never lose an email after it is sent.

## Expected outcome

The send-once guarantee email is missing today, ready for the scheduled sender and available to any later email path that needs it.

## Implementation context

One of four slices delivering Send an email later from the CRM. This is deliberately only the half that runs before the provider is contacted: the half that runs after, recording a confirmed email into CRM, already exists. Mirror the equivalent texting work in Prevent duplicate SMS sends with durable idempotency rather than inventing a second shape.

Detailed point-in-time implementation planning, including the full itemised in-scope and out-of-scope lists, is in AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Prevent duplicate SMS sends with durable idempotency
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Context

ENG-12251 and ENG-12301 moved Acquisity SMS sends onto a shared send-and-record path. That gives us one place to add protection, but it does not yet guarantee that a retried request, concurrent workflow or timeout will send only once.

A Twilio timeout is especially dangerous: Twilio may have accepted the SMS even when Acquisity did not receive the response. Blindly retrying can send the prospect the same text twice.

## Outcome

Each intended SMS send reaches Twilio at most once, while genuine new messages—including messages with the same wording—can still be sent normally.

## Scope

* Give every manual, workflow, automated and scheduled SMS operation a durable business-operation key.
* Claim the operation atomically before calling the provider so concurrent attempts cannot both send.
* Reuse the existing result when the same operation is retried.
* Persist the Twilio MessageSid and recorded CRM message against the operation.
* Treat provider timeouts and other ambiguous responses as unknown, not failed.
* Reconcile an unknown result before any resend; never blindly resend after an ambiguous provider response.
* Use a recoverable lease/state model so a crash before the provider call does not leave the message permanently stuck.
* Keep idempotency scoped to the intended operation, not phone number plus message body, because users may legitimately send the same wording again later.
* Apply the protection in the shared send path so no screen or workflow bypasses it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Two concurrent attempts for the same send operation call Twilio once and create one CRM message.
2. Retrying the same workflow step or API mutation returns the original result without sending again.
3. A crash after Twilio accepts the message but before local bookkeeping does not cause a blind resend.
4. An ambiguous timeout is recorded as unknown and reconciled before any further send attempt.
5. A crash after claiming but before calling Twilio can recover safely without remaining stuck forever.
6. Two intentional sends with identical recipient and body but different operation keys are both allowed.
7. Manual, workflow, automated and scheduled SMS paths all use the same protection.
8. Tests cover concurrent attempts, retries, pre-send failure, post-acceptance failure and ambiguous provider timeout.
9. Production monitoring can identify duplicate attempts, unknown outcomes and recovered sends without exposing message content.

## Related work

* ENG-12251 created the shared send-and-record path.
* ENG-12301 moved the remaining SMS procedure onto that path.
* ENG-11728 contains similar safety principles for email but does not cover SMS.
* ENG-12269 will add scheduled and higher-volume automated texting.

Engineering planning must confirm the operation-key contract and recovery design against current main before implementation.

relatedSnapshot.title: Add feature to Schedule texts and emails
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Reps can choose a future time for a CRM text or email, trust that it will send once, see what is waiting, and cancel it before sending starts.

## Problem

CRM messages currently send immediately. Reps cannot prepare a message while the conversation is fresh and have CRM deliver it at the right time later. There is also no single place showing what is scheduled or whether it eventually sent.

## Proposed fix

Add one shared scheduled-message system for CRM texts and emails. Each scheduled message has a saved send time and visible status. At the scheduled time, CRM re-checks that the rep, sender and recipient are still allowed, then uses the normal recorded sending path.

## What's included

1. Send one text later.
2. Send an email later from CRM.
3. Show and cancel scheduled messages.

Later automation, sequences, quiet hours, editing, bulk actions and automatic call tasks remain in Automated communication follow-ups. They do not block this release.

## Execution order

Use the lowest numbered eligible ticket first.

### Wave 1: shared foundation and scheduled SMS

1. Send one text later creates the shared scheduled-message record and worker, then makes one CRM text send later.

### Wave 2: scheduled email

2. Send an email later from CRM starts after the shared foundation and reliable sent-email storage.

### Wave 3: management and cancellation

3. Show and cancel scheduled messages starts after both channel implementations exist.

Safe parallel work: none verified. The children share saved state, the background worker, API and composer behaviour.

## How it should work

* Save the message and scheduled time before background work begins.
* Store the chosen time as an absolute timestamp and display it in the user's current timezone with the timezone shown.
* At send time, re-check membership, permission, sender ownership or mailbox access, sender connection and recipient opt-out state.
* Use one durable operation key per scheduled message so retries cannot create a second delivery.
* Treat database status as authoritative.
* Cancellation succeeds only while the message is pending.
* Show pending, sending, sent, cancelled, failed and unknown states truthfully.
* An ambiguous provider result becomes unknown and is reconciled instead of blindly sent again.

## Who can do what

* A rep can schedule a channel only when they can send through it now.
* The creator can view and cancel their pending messages.
* Managers can view and cancel messages covered by their existing team communication scope.
* Losing permission, membership, mailbox access or phone-number ownership before execution prevents delivery.

## What the user sees

* Send now or Send later in the existing text and email composers.
* A date, time and timezone confirmation.
* A clear success message showing when the message is due.
* A Scheduled messages view with recipient, channel, creator, send time and status.
* Plain failure reasons and a clear too-late-to-cancel result.

## Done when

- [ ] A rep can schedule one CRM text and one Gmail or Microsoft email.
- [ ] Each message sends no more than once.
- [ ] Every successful send appears once in the correct CRM history.
- [ ] Permission, sender access and opt-out are rechecked immediately before sending.
- [ ] A pending message can be cancelled and never sends during a retry.
- [ ] Browser QA covers both composers, timezone display, list, cancellation and recovery.
- [ ] Activation events are verified in PostHog.

## Open questions

None at master level. Child tickets contain the remaining bounded decisions and recommended defaults.

## Expected outcome

A rep can prepare a message now and rely on CRM to deliver it later without duplicate sends, silent failures or hidden scheduled work.

## Implementation context

Use one CRM-owned scheduled-message model and worker for both channels. Do not reuse the AI SDR scheduled-followup table, which represents automated sequences and has a different lifecycle.

relatedSnapshot.title: Stop mailbox sync adding a second copy of emails already imported from Close
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

An email that was imported from Close can show twice on a person: once as imported history and once as a copy the connected Gmail mailbox syncs in later. Mailbox sync should recognise the imported email and not add a second copy.

## Problem

The Close import already skips any email the mailbox sync stored first. The reverse is not protected. When the sync later stores an email that was imported, it does not see the imported copy, so it saves its own in a new conversation. The rep then sees the same email twice on the person's timeline and in Conversations, and an old sent email appears as a new unread conversation.

First seen on 1 Oct 2026 in the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace: two emails sent on 19 Sep were imported at 12:15 UTC and stored again by the sync at 14:10 UTC.

## User experience

* A rep opens a person whose email history came from Close. Each email shows once.
* Something later makes the CRM look up that person's past mail in the reps' inboxes (the person gets a new email address, an automation updates them, or a new mailbox is connected). Today the same email appears a second time. Expected: nothing new appears for emails that are already there as imported history.
* New mail that was never imported still syncs in as normal.

Who is affected: any workspace with both imported email history and connected mailboxes. Today that is the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace.

## Proposed fix

When the mailbox sync is about to save an email, it checks whether the same person already has an imported email with the same Message-ID. If so, it skips that email and leaves the imported copy untouched. This applies to every way mail reaches the CRM from a connected Gmail or Outlook mailbox: live sync, the first 90-day import, the catch-up after a sync gap, the lookup of a person's past emails, and the refresh of a conversation after a rep sends from it.

## What's included

* The skip rule above for Gmail and Outlook mailboxes.
* A send from the app that was written in an imported conversation starts a live mailbox conversation on the same person, instead of being filed on the imported one.

After this ships, as a separate step: a read-only dry run that lists the pairs that already exist, and then their removal. Removal needs James's decision on which copy stays, a restore procedure proven on a non-production copy, his explicit approval, and a window agreed with the Close import.

Not included: joining imported history and live mail into one conversation, a database uniqueness rule on Message-ID (the same Message-ID legitimately repeats when one email went to several people), and changes to the Close import itself.

## How it should work

* Same person and same Message-ID: the sync skips the email. No second copy, no new conversation, no unread flag.
* Name 1 on a different person: both people keep their own copy, as today.
* Emails without a Message-ID save as they do today.
* The imported copy is never changed by the sync. It does not gain mailbox details, so deleting the email in Gmail later does not remove the imported history.
* If a batch contains both imported and new emails, only the new ones are saved, and conversation counts reflect what was saved.
* Replays and retries create no duplicates.
* The Message-ID comparison ignores letter case and surrounding spaces, as the Close import's own check does.
* An imported conversation never becomes the home of live mailbox mail. If a rep sends from the app while in an imported conversation, the sent email goes on a live mailbox conversation, so the customer's reply shows as needing a reply.
* A mailbox save and an import of the same email cannot run at the same moment: both wait on the same lock for that email's Message-ID.

## Done when

- [ ] Triggering a past-email lookup for a person with imported emails adds no second copy of those emails.
- [ ] Connecting a new mailbox does not duplicate imported emails for people who have them.
- [ ] An email sent to two people, imported on one of them, still syncs onto the other.
- [ ] New, never-imported mail still syncs and shows as before.
- [ ] Imported emails are unchanged after a sync touches the same mail.
- [ ] A send from the app that names an imported conversation lands on a live mailbox conversation, and the imported conversation is unchanged.

Not part of this ticket's code change: listing and removing the pairs that already exist (see What's included).

## Implementation context

* The sync's duplicate check only matches rows the Gmail (or Outlook) sync wrote itself, and only inside the conversation it resolved, so imported rows are invisible to it. The same holds for how it picks a conversation by headers.
* The job that wrote the first two pairs was the lookup of a person's past emails, which runs when a person is created or their email address is added or changed, including by automations. Its own "already stored" check also only knows Gmail ids.
* Read-only production counts on 1 Oct 2026 (Sales Team workspace): 2 pairs visible by Message-ID; at least 51 more where the older synced copy has no stored Message-ID (114 probable); 1,226 imported emails with an unsynced copy waiting in a connected mailbox, growing while the import finishes.
* The check is driven by the person's own conversations through existing indexes, with the Message-ID compared trimmed and lower-cased. No new index or migration. Measured on the production replica: 1.7 ms for the first affected person, 92 ms cold for the person with the most imported email. Inside the import, 2,459 Message-IDs repeat across 10,621 rows, 1,156 of them across different people, which is why the rule is scoped to the person and why a unique index is not safe.
* Builds on Show one conversation when several reps got the same email and Find a new contact's past emails in every rep's inbox. The imported history comes from Close migration: conversations, calls, notes, tasks and meetings (wave 5).

relatedSnapshot.title: Close CRM and Email inbox/sync parity
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Goal

Match Close for connected Gmail and Microsoft email: automatic history, reliable replies and a clear inbox.

**Owner:** Ebubeker Rexha · **Priority:** High
**37 sub-issues:** 20 open or coordinating tickets, 17 completed.

## Start here

Finish the in-progress reconnect work first. With extra capacity, work on Recall safety and notifications alongside it.

**The numbers are pickup order, not extra blockers.** Start a ticket as soon as its actual dependencies are complete.

## Execution order

### 1. Start now · parallel

1. **Show clear reconnect messages** · ENG-13542
2. **Finish Recall scheduling safety** · ENG-13547
3. **Build notification delivery** · ENG-13431

**Parallel:** these cover separate UI, Recall and notification areas. Keep one writer for any shared mailbox helper.

### 2. Continue each lane independently

4. **Finish Recall completion safety** · ENG-13548
   After: ENG-13547.
5. **Add email reply alerts** · ENG-13433
   After: ENG-13431.

**Parallel:** these two can overlap. Recall completion must follow scheduling. Email alert integration can start now, but each provider must pass sync QA before its alerts are enabled.

**Binding checkpoints:** finish ENG-13438 and ENG-12668 once their remaining acceptance criteria pass.

### 3. Build provider sync · Gmail and Microsoft can overlap

6. **Import Gmail history** · ENG-13525
   After: ENG-13438; keep the Gmail programme's ENG-12668 gate.
7. **Build Microsoft sync** · ENG-12972
   After: ENG-12668.
8. **Keep new Gmail messages flowing** · ENG-13528
   After: ENG-13525.
9. **Show Gmail health and finish live QA** · ENG-13529
   After: ENG-13528.

**Gmail is one chain:** 6 → 8 → 9.
**Parallel:** Microsoft (7) can run alongside that chain once the shared sync contract is settled. Email alerts (5) can also progress. Serialize shared schema, persistence and settings edits.

**Sync checkpoints:** verify ENG-2061 and ENG-12256 after their provider acceptance passes.

### 4. Finish the shared email paths · sequential by default

10. **Make email views read stored data only** · ENG-12690
    After: ENG-2061 and ENG-12972.
11. **Link mail to existing CRM records** · ENG-12669
    After: ENG-12668 and ENG-12256.
12. **Recover sent email without sending twice** · ENG-12569
    After: ENG-12256.
13. **Create appropriate People from conversations** · ENG-12670
    After: ENG-12668 and ENG-12256.

**Parallel:** none verified for these shared email routes and persistence changes. Use the order above when multiple tickets are eligible. Contact creation (13) does not block ordinary inbox/reply delivery.

### 5. Add email to Conversations

14. **Show email threads and support replies** · ENG-13342
    After: ENG-12256 and ENG-12569.

**Parallel:** can overlap unfinished email alerts (5), with one agreed conversation link and sender contract. Serialize shared unread/reply-state edits.

Alerts can use the existing authorized email screen before this new Conversations screen is ready.

## Name 3 checkpoints

These coordinate acceptance; they are not extra implementations to repeat:

* ENG-12664 · overall reliable inbox sync.
* ENG-12668 · safe mailbox/workspace access.
* ENG-13438 · remaining Gmail binding and Recall safety.
* ENG-12256 · both providers meet the shared sync contract.
* ENG-2061 · Gmail import, live updates and health.
* ENG-12970 · later inbox controls; keep scoped follow-ups separate from basic sync.

## Already in progress

* ENG-13542 · reconnect explanations.
* ENG-13438 · Gmail binding programme.
* ENG-12668 · mailbox workspace programme.

The Recall delivery tickets remain Todo until work is actually started.

## Completed · keep Done

### Mailbox foundations

* ENG-13437 · workspace binding records.
* ENG-13439 · Outlook workspace enforcement.
* ENG-13541 · recovery for missing bindings.

### Scheduled email

* ENG-12973 · scheduled email programme.
* ENG-13223 · durable scheduled email.
* ENG-13224 · duplicate-send protection.
* ENG-13226 · scheduled sending programme.
* ENG-13227 · scheduling from the contact record.
* ENG-13288 · blocked-recipient protection.
* ENG-13289 · send-time authorization checks.
* ENG-13290 · send once and record the result.

### Scheduled-message management

* ENG-12975 · management and cancellation programme.
* ENG-13343 · truthful cancellation eligibility.
* ENG-13344 · permission-safe message lists.
* ENG-13345 · safe cancellation.
* ENG-13346 · reusable status components.
* ENG-13347 · CRM management screen.

Done reflects current Name 2 status, not a new live-mailbox QA pass. Do not reopen scheduled email because general immediate-send recovery remains unfinished.

## Remaining parity gaps

These still need focused delivery scope. They are not new tickets yet.

- [ ] Older and archived contact history, including later contact backfill.
- [ ] Internal/private email exclusions before sharing imported mail.
- [ ] Personal Done/archive sync, preserving CRM history.
- [ ] Snooze and no-reply reminders.
- [ ] Incoming/outgoing attachment support.
- [ ] Verified aliases and delegated sending.
- [ ] Private Add/Discard review for unknown contacts.

Use the existing follow-up and matching scope before creating duplicates. Later controls must not block the basic sync release through a blanket dependency.

## Completion checklist

- [ ] Gmail and Microsoft stay current without opening CRM.
- [ ] Customer-started mail and external/mobile sends appear correctly.
- [ ] Matching, participant privacy and deduplication are verified.
- [ ] Send recovery never repeats a confirmed or ambiguous send.
- [ ] Sync health, reconnect and disconnect behave truthfully.
- [ ] Reps can find and reply to emails in Conversations.
- [ ] New replies notify the correct rep without duplicate or historic alerts.
- [ ] Every remaining parity gap has verified delivery or an explicit scope decision.
- [ ] Both providers pass live QA for the delivered behavior.

## Organization

All 37 tracked tickets are direct sub-issues here, as requested. Their previous programme parents remain related links for context. Existing blockers, assignees, priorities and statuses are preserved. Broader Conversations and notification masters remain separate.

## Scope notes

Done/archive means “handled”: remove an email from the rep's actionable inbox and archive their own provider copy, while retaining CRM history. Provider archive changes should also clear the Acquisity action item. Read, Done and delete are separate actions; another recipient's work must not be cleared.

The initial target is Gmail/Microsoft. Custom IMAP/SMTP, bulk email, tracking and snippets require separate scope decisions. No trial or Close cutover is scheduled by this ticket.

## Evidence

Close configuration · Close Inbox · Email filtering · Name 4

AI context.md

relatedSnapshot.title: Send desktop notifications for new texts when every Acquisity tab is closed
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A rep who has turned on closed-tab notifications in a browser gets a desktop notification for a new client text even when every Acquisity tab is closed. Clicking it reopens the right workspace and conversation.

## Problem

Name 5 notifications only appear while an Acquisity tab is open. Reps who close the app miss client replies until they come back.

## Proposed fix

Register a browser for closed-tab notifications when the person opts in, and send each new text notification to that browser through standard web push. Open tabs and the closed-tab notification never both alert for the same item.

## What's included

* Saving a browser subscription for the signed-in person, and removing it.
* A background worker in the browser that shows the notification and handles the click.
* Sending for new text notifications only. Missed calls and failed texts join when their own notifications ship (ENG-13780, ENG-13853).
* A simple Turn on and Turn off control so the slice can be tested end to end. The full design comes in Show and manage closed-tab notifications.
* Not included: native mobile app push (ENG-15169), answering calls with the app closed.

## Blocked by

* None: can start immediately.

## How it should work

* One interruption: if an Acquisity tab is open in that browser, the tab's own alert wins and the closed-tab notification replaces it rather than adding a second one.
* Each person's Name 5 choice for Text replies and their quiet hours apply.
* Lock-screen text stays minimal: who texted and in which workspace, not the message body.
* Access is checked before sending and again when the notification is clicked.
* Notifications expire if the browser cannot receive them for a while, and several texts close together are grouped.
* Subscriptions the browser service reports as gone are deleted.
* Signing out, switching account, being removed from the workspace, or turning it off stops delivery to that browser.
* The setting is off until a person turns it on.

## Who can do what

* A person can only add or remove their own browsers.
* A browser only receives notifications for workspaces its person still belongs to and items they can see.

## What the user sees

* After turning on, a new text shows an operating-system notification with the app closed. Clicking it opens Acquisity on that conversation.
* If the person can no longer see it, the click opens their notifications with a short message instead.

## Done when

- [ ] On a supported browser with all Acquisity tabs closed, a new text shows a real operating-system notification and clicking it opens the right workspace and conversation.
- [ ] With a tab open, the same text alerts exactly once.
- [ ] Turning off, signing out on a shared device, losing workspace access, and an expired subscription each stop delivery.
- [ ] Tests separate the push service accepting the message, the browser receiving it, the notification being shown, and the person opening it.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Reps stop missing client texts because the Acquisity tab was closed.

## Implementation context

* Needs a web push key pair added to the environment for preview and production; the slice stays switched off until the keys exist.
* The desktop notification tags already used by open tabs are the shared key for the one-interruption rule.
* AI context.md

relatedSnapshot.title: Master: Conversations stays fast with full Close history
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Conversations should open in under a second for the AI Acquisition Sales Team, even after the Close import adds about 440k calls, 1.4M texts and 790k emails. Today every list, count and unread badge rebuilds the whole workspace's history before showing 50 rows, so its cost grows with total history.

## Problem

The inbox builds every call, text thread and email thread in the workspace on every load: about 6,600 today, taking about 0.3 seconds after ENG-14300. The Close history takes that to about 190,000 for people already in Acquisity and about 670,000 in total. That points to roughly 9 to 30 seconds per load. In CRM v2 workspaces the sidebar's unread count re-runs this every 60 seconds for every rep (ENG-14327), and a 9,900-call test slice on 28 Sep added about a second to every list and count load.

Every fast inbox we looked at (Close, HubSpot, Front, Missive, Slack, Name 2) keeps one ready row per conversation, updated as messages arrive, and pages over that. Research: Making Conversations fast at Close scale.

## What's included

* Quick guards so Conversations stays responsive while the redesign is built: one shared cached count for the sidebar and the page's counts, and a 90-day window for calls and texts in the list.
* A maintained inbox table: one ready row per person, updated when a call, text or email is saved.
* Conversations reading that table for the list, counts, badge and My Day Replies.
* Opening a person and their timeline staying fast with years of history.
* Not included: the Close importer's own rules (import flags, real call times). Those stay with the Close migration work.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Tickets grouped as parallel may start together when there is capacity, but they keep the priority order below. Waves show the earliest unlock, not a barrier.

### Wave 1: can start now

Parallel: ENG-14373 (once its outside blocker ENG-14327 merges), ENG-14369, ENG-14370 and ENG-14371.

1. Conversations reuses the sidebar's unread count instead of counting again: the v2 sidebar count and the page's chip counts share one cached count. Blocked by ENG-14327 (outside this master). Client-side only, so it does not collide with ENG-14369.
2. Show calls and texts from the last 90 days in the Conversations list: old calls and texts leave the list.
3. Keep a ready inbox row per person, updated as messages are saved: the inbox table, read markers, backfill and nightly repair.
4. Opening a person in Conversations stays fast with years of history: timeline measured at volume and paged.

### Wave 2: starts when ENG-14370 is done

Parallel: none.

5. Conversations loads from the ready inbox table at any volume: blocked by ENG-14370.

Cross-wave overlap:

* ENG-14372 may start when ENG-14370 completes, and may overlap ENG-14371 if it is still underway.

## Done when

* Conversations list, counts and badge each return in under 500 ms on production for the Sales Team workspace with the full Close history loaded.
* Opening a person with the most imported history takes under 500 ms.
* Load time no longer grows with total history, measured before and after a bulk load.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR adds follow-up after decline; investigate classification/thread
relatedSnapshot.description:
In a prospect decline scenario, the AI replied with: `I follow up after "XY" date ???`.

Expected behavior: send a polite thank-you and cancel follow-ups.

Notes from discussion:

* Possible confusion between decline vs deferral patterns in the AI SDR prompt.
* Escalation did not trigger; SDR workflow appears to have missed part of the thread, so the "decline" message may not have been ingested.

Reference: see the Inngest run linked below.

User impact:

User gets frustrated because when he wrote "DECLINE" the SDR did not send just a polite thank You note, but incorrectly suggested that it will follow up (activating the future deferral pattern).

Root cause:

Future deferral should be an escalation intent, not a different mail type.

Solution:

* Need to investigate why the extended escalationdetector did not caught this intent.

relatedSnapshot.title: Floor Command: load the HT Sales dashboard in a few seconds instead of 20
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Switching Floor Command to the HT Sales view takes about 21 seconds before the numbers appear, and LT Sales takes about 5. Managers should see their dashboard within a few seconds on every view.

## Problem

Measured on production in the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace on 17 September 2026, last 30 days with previous period:

* HT Sales (17 reps): the main report request alone took 18.3s. The whole view took about 21s.
* LT Sales (11 reps): about 4.8s in total, with the main report fetched twice in a row while switching views.
* The main report is also the building block for every metric detail window, so its speed multiplies there too.

The likely slow parts are payment lookups that read across the workspace's entire payment history instead of only the selected dates and deals. This needs confirming with query plans before changing anything.

## User experience

A manager opens Floor Command or switches reporting view. Cards and the closer table fill in within a few seconds on HT Sales and about a second on LT Sales. Switching view fires the report once, not twice. Every number stays exactly as it is today.

## What's included

* Profile the main report (`getFloorCommandReport`) for HT Sales against the read-only production replica and fix the queries that dominate.
* Likely candidates, to confirm with query plans first: the upsell contract average lookup over all received payments, the buyer history lookup, and the cash category lookups repeated per report.
* Add or adjust indexes only where the query plan proves they are needed.
* Stop the report being requested twice when switching view.
* Not included: metric detail window speed (ENG-13942), page loading states, any change to metric definitions.

## Done when

* On production, AI Acquisition Sales Team, last 30 days with previous period: HT Sales main report returns in under 4s and LT Sales in under 1.5s.
* Switching reporting view requests the main report once.
* Before and after query plans for the changed queries are attached to the PR.
* A regression test shows the report output for a fixture workspace is unchanged.

## Implementation context

Measurements and suspected hot spots: AI context.md.

Sibling ticket for metric detail speed: ENG-13942.

relatedSnapshot.title: Format emails, write long texts and see scheduled messages in Conversations
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

In Conversations, reps can format emails the way they do in Gmail and write long texts in a box that grows or opens larger. They can also see and cancel their scheduled emails and texts right in the conversation.

## Problem

* The Conversations email box is plain text: no bold, lists, links or text size.
* The text box is three lines tall, so long texts are hard to write and check.
* A scheduled email or text only shows on the separate Scheduled page. A rep reading the thread cannot see that something is about to go out, or stop it.

## User experience

**Email**

* A formatting bar sits under the email text, in Gmail's order:
  * undo, redo
  * text size (Small, Normal, Large, Huge)
  * bold, italic, underline, strikethrough
  * text colour, link
  * numbered and bulleted lists, quote, align, clear formatting
* When the composer is narrow, the least-used controls fold into More.
* A Formatting button hides or shows the bar.
* The full email editor has the same bar, and formatting carries between the two.
* Usual shortcuts work: ⌘B, ⌘I, ⌘U, and ⌘K for a link.

**Texts**

* The text box grows with the message up to about a third of the screen, then scrolls.
* The expand button opens a larger editor with the same draft.
* The counter explains segments in words, including when an emoji makes the text cost more.
* Texts stay plain text: there is no bold or italic on texts.

**Scheduled messages**

* Each scheduled email or text for this person shows after the newest message, with a dashed outline. It shows who scheduled it, the message and when it will send.
* Cancel send appears only while it can still be cancelled.
* A message that is already sending, or being checked, says so in words.
* A failed one shows the reason.

## What's included

* The Conversations email composer (docked and full editor) and the Conversations text composer.
* Scheduled messages on the person's thread. They follow the same visibility rules as the Scheduled page, plus access to that person.
* Tracking: send events record whether the email was formatted, and cancelling from the thread is tracked.

Not included:

* email attachments (ENG-13827, the next PR)
* editing or retrying a scheduled message (ENG-14176)
* the scheduled count on the Scheduled button (ENG-14171)
* the record page's text box
* bold or italic in texts

## How it should work

* Email formatting is kept when the email is sent. The same formatting shows in the thread, in light and dark mode, including italics.
* Only simple formatting is kept: size, colour from the bar's palette, and alignment. Styles pasted from other emails do not change how received mail looks.
* Signatures (ENG-13828), merge variables (ENG-13831), templates and replies keep working with the formatted editor.
* A saved draft reopens with its formatting. Older plain drafts still open.
* Texts warn before the 1,600-character limit, and Send is disabled above it.

## Who can do what

* A rep sees a scheduled message on a thread only if they could see it on the Scheduled page and can open that person.
* Only people allowed to cancel it on the Scheduled page can cancel it from the thread.

## Done when

* A formatted email (bold, italic, list, link, size, colour) arrives formatted in Gmail and Outlook, and shows the same in the thread in light and dark mode.
* Signatures, variables, templates and replies still work, and send once.
* A long text grows and scrolls, opens in the larger editor, and sends the same draft.
* A scheduled message shows on the thread and can be cancelled there. A message that has started sending cannot be cancelled and says why.
* A rep cannot see scheduled messages they would not see on the Scheduled page, or for a person they cannot access.
* Tracking events are confirmed landing in PostHog from the preview.
* QA runs on a preview workspace with test mailboxes. No production sends.

## Design

Kit (full design): `#/screen/crm-conversations`, composer design pass of 29 Sep 2026. Screenshots are attached to this ticket. The production cut hides Edit and Retry on scheduled messages (ENG-14176).

## Implementation context

This is high risk: it changes outbound email content, the shared email display policy, and adds a new person-scoped read of scheduled messages. The scheduled-messages part is the slice of ENG-14168 that does not need its events read.

Full point-in-time context: AI context.md.
